en.title: Shia LaBeouf's 'Even Stevens' Rivalry With 'Lizzie McGuire' Revealed
en.summary: Christy Carlson Romano spills the tea on a young Shia LaBeouf's competitive streak, revealing he trash-talked 'Lizzie McGuire' to boost 'Even Stevens'. The 'Even Stevens' star wanted his show to reign supreme on Disney Channel.
en.body:
Remember the golden age of Disney Channel, when **Even Stevens** and **Lizzie McGuire** battled for ratings supremacy? Well, it turns out the competition wasn't just on screen. **Christy Carlson Romano**, who starred as Ren Stevens, recently shared that her co-star, **Shia LaBeouf**, was intensely competitive and actively trash-talked the rival show, **Lizzie McGuire**, while they were filming.

Romano recalled on "The Joe Vulpis Podcast" that LaBeouf was determined for **Even Stevens** to be the number one show on the network. This ambition fueled a "beef" with **Lizzie McGuire**'s star, **Hilary Duff**, though Romano emphasized that Duff was likely unaware of LaBeouf's specific comments. LaBeouf's focus was squarely on making **Even Stevens** a hit, to the point where he'd actively disparage the competition during their own production.

> "He wanted to be the number one show... He was definitely beefing with Hilary Duff... Hilary had no clue about that. I'm sure she was doing her own thing, but he would always be kind of trash-talking Lizzie McGuire."

— Christy Carlson Romano

This revelation adds a layer of behind-the-scenes drama to the nostalgic memories of these beloved sitcoms. For fans who grew up watching both **Even Stevens** and **Lizzie McGuire**, this insight into LaBeouf's competitive spirit offers a new perspective on the era. It highlights the intense pressure on young actors and the drive to succeed in a crowded entertainment landscape. The fact that LaBeouf's ambition was directed towards outperforming a direct competitor, even through vocal criticism, speaks volumes about his early determination and showmanship. It’s a reminder that the magic seen on screen often comes with intense effort and a fierce will to win.

## The Stakes of Network Dominance

In the cutthroat world of children's television, being the number one show meant everything. For Disney Channel, having a flagship series like **Even Stevens** or **Lizzie McGuire** at the top of the ratings translated to more merchandise, more brand recognition, and greater opportunities for its stars. **Shia LaBeouf**'s alleged trash-talking wasn't just idle chatter; it was a strategic (albeit immature) tactic to motivate himself and his castmates, aiming to ensure their show outperformed its biggest rival. This competitive fire, as described by Romano, likely contributed to the energy and success that made **Even Stevens** a memorable part of early 2000s television culture.

## What's Next for These Stars

While **Shia LaBeouf** and **Christy Carlson Romano** have both moved on to vastly different and often complex careers in Hollywood, this anecdote serves as a fun, nostalgic look back at their Disney Channel origins. **Hilary Duff** continues to star in the successful **How I Met Your Father** on Hulu, proving her lasting appeal. LaBeouf's career has seen him transition from child star to critically acclaimed actor, while Romano has embraced a multifaceted career including podcasting and acting.
